stories.head: Coveo Acquires Anglera to Bring Agentic Product Data Enrichment to AI-Powered eCommerce
stories.plain: Coveo bought Anglera, a Y Combinator-backed startup whose agentic product data enrichment engine automatically cleans and structures catalog data. The combined platform helps retailers surface products inside AI shopping assistants as well as their own sites. This matters because clean, structured product data is fast becoming the key lever for winning placement in AI-generated shopping results.

stories.head: DV Research: 97% of Marketers Plan to Use AI, but Workflow Adoption Remains Uneven
stories.plain: DoubleVerify's 2026 Global Insights Report finds near-universal intent to adopt AI in marketing, yet actual deployment across advertising workflows is patchy. Marketers cite accuracy and effectiveness as top concerns when evaluating tools. The gap between aspiration and implementation signals a governance and measurement problem more than a technology gap — critical context for anyone buying or building MarTech-AI.

stories.head: 8×8 Platform Update: Build an AI Agent Once, Deploy Across Every Channel with Full Customer History
stories.plain: 8×8 updated its CX platform so teams can build one AI agent and deploy it across multiple channels, while keeping the full customer history visible in a single view synced to the CRM. This reduces duplicated bot-building effort and makes cross-channel context consistent — a practical step toward true agentic decisioning at scale.

stories.head: Martech Signal Economics: Which Customer Signals Are Actually Worth Paying For?
stories.plain: This analysis tackles a foundational budgeting question: with signals coming from web visits, app activity, email, search, and transactions, which ones genuinely improve AI-driven decisions and which just add cost and noise? Understanding signal value directly shapes how CDPs are configured and how much personalization and decisioning models actually learn — essential framing for anyone specifying a stack.

stories.head: Vusion Completes Acquisition of In-Store Media to Expand AI-Powered Retail Media into Physical Stores
stories.plain: Vusion has closed its purchase of In-Store Media, merging connected-store shelf technology with retail media expertise. The deal extends AI-driven ad decisioning into physical retail environments, creating a new channel where brands can bid for placement triggered by real-world shopper behavior. It signals that retail media networks are moving beyond the screen into bricks-and-mortar.

stories.head: Cordial Launches Headless CDP, Bringing Real-Time Customer Data to Where Marketers Work
stories.plain: Cordial has made its embedded CDP headless, meaning marketers can pull real-time customer data directly into the AI assistants and tools they already use instead of logging into a separate platform. This shifts the CDP from a destination to an infrastructure layer — a significant architectural move that changes how personalization gets built and bought.

stories.head: Coveo Acquires Anglera to Make Product Data a Competitive Advantage in AI-Powered eCommerce
stories.plain: Coveo bought Anglera, an AI-native startup that automatically enriches product catalog data, and will fold it into its experience platform. Agentic product data enrichment means AI shopping assistants get cleaner, richer inputs — directly affecting how well products surface in both on-site search and AI-powered shopping agents. A structural bet on data quality as competitive moat.

stories.head: Contentstack Canoe Shows Brands How AI Engines Describe Them — and What to Fix
stories.plain: Contentstack's Canoe tool lets marketers see exactly how ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude describe their brand, which sources get cited, and where gaps exist. This is a practical, hands-on demo of Generative Engine Optimization — making your brand visible inside AI answers — a discipline that is fast becoming a buying priority for content and SEO teams.

stories.head: DV Research: 97% of Marketers Plan to Use AI, but Adoption Across Advertising Workflows Remains Uneven
stories.plain: DoubleVerify's 2026 Global Insights Report finds near-universal AI intent among marketers but uneven real-world adoption, with accuracy and effectiveness topping evaluation criteria. The data matters because it maps where buying dollars and governance scrutiny are actually concentrating — useful for anyone building or selling AI into advertising and media workflows.

stories.head: Martech Signal Economics: Which Customer Signals Are Actually Worth Paying For?
stories.plain: A practical analysis of how to evaluate the ROI of customer signals — from web visits to transaction data — asking which ones genuinely improve decisions versus adding noise and cost. As signal costs rise and privacy rules tighten, understanding signal economics is foundational for anyone governing a CDP or tuning an AI decisioning layer.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Adoption Is Wide but Uneven in Practice
body: Almost every marketer now says they plan to use AI, yet DV Research finds that actual deployment is concentrated in a handful of tasks while most advertising workflows remain untouched. The gap between intent and implementation is the real story — not the headline adoption number.

This uneven pattern shows up elsewhere: iCIMS is rebranding its entire enterprise around AI, but deliberately signals who the product is not for, acknowledging that blanket AI positioning no longer differentiates. Decisions about where to deploy AI, and where to hold back, are becoming the core strategic choice.

themes.head: Agentic Marketing Moves From Concept to Case Study
body: The 2026 Contentstack Experience Award winners show that agentic marketing — AI systems that act autonomously across content, data, and customer touchpoints — is no longer theoretical. Real brands are running live deployments, and the lessons are concrete enough to benchmark against.

Security teams are feeling the pressure too: AI agent access has jumped to the top of 2026 access-control priorities. Governance of autonomous agents, not just their capabilities, is emerging as the operational frontier that separates early adopters from organizations that scale safely.
ev: Agile Brand · AI agent access security

themes.head: Data Infrastructure Gets Headless & Composable
body: Cordial's headless CDP launch is a signal of a broader architectural shift: rather than forcing marketers into a single platform, vendors are now pushing data to wherever work already happens. The competitive advantage moves from the platform itself to how cleanly it integrates with existing stacks.

Coveo's acquisition of Anglera reinforces this: the prize is product data quality that can feed any AI-powered commerce surface, not ownership of the front-end experience. Signal economics — knowing which customer data is actually worth collecting and paying for — is becoming a distinct strategic discipline.

themes.head: Purpose-Built AI Replaces General-Purpose Platforms
body: Conga embedding GC AI directly into contract lifecycle management, and Practifi deepening a purpose-built CRM for wealth management, illustrate a decisive trend: vertical-specific AI trained on domain data is displacing generic tools that required heavy customisation. The value proposition is narrower scope, faster time-to-value, and lower hallucination risk.

Aurora Mobile's Modellix.ai takes a different angle — unified access to multiple specialist models inside creative workflows — suggesting that even within 'general' creative tools, the architecture underneath is becoming a curated mix of purpose-built models. The era of one-model-fits-all is quietly ending.
ev: Agile Brand · Conga + GC AI legal

themes.head: Physical & Digital Retail Media Converge In-Store
body: Vusion's acquisition of In-Store Media brings programmatic retail-media logic — targeting, measurement, real-time optimisation — into physical store environments. This collapses the long-standing boundary between digital advertising and the shelf, making the store itself a trackable media channel.

Combined with AI-powered eCommerce data plays like Coveo-Anglera, a unified commerce-media layer is forming where the same customer signal can inform a digital ad, an on-shelf display, and a personalised recommendation simultaneously. Brands that treat online and offline media budgets as separate are increasingly working with an outdated model.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the defining move is the same: generic, broad-scope tools are being replaced by purpose-built, data-specific, composable systems — and the organisations that grasp this architectural shift first will set the competitive baseline for everyone else.
